Work ranges from traffic and pavement design to network operations and infrastructure planning.

label: Hydraulic Engineering
summary: Hydraulic engineering is the sub-discipline of civil engineering concerned with the flow and conveyance of fluids, principally water. Wikipedia states that "hydraulic engineering as a sub-discipline of civil engineering is concerned with the flow and conveyance of fluids, principally water and sewage." The field applies fluid mechanics and hydrology to the design of dams, canals, levees, pipelines, pumping stations, drainage networks, and water- and wastewater-treatment infrastructure. ASCE's Environmental and Water Resources Institute, founded in 1999, frames its mission as "advancing water resources and environmental solutions to achieve a sustainable future" and serves as a technical source for environmental and water-related issues. The Library of Congress Classification gives hydraulic engineering its own top-level technology heading, with technical practice classified under "Technical hydraulics." Practitioners manage water supply, flood control, irrigation, and energy generation systems.

label: Construction Engineering and Management
summary: Construction engineering and management is the sub-discipline of civil engineering that deals with the planning, methods, and management of building and infrastructure projects. Wikipedia describes construction engineering as a "professional sub-discipline of civil engineering that deals with the designing, planning, construction, and operations management of infrastructure such as roadways, tunnels, bridges, airports, railroads, facilities, buildings, dams, utilities and other projects." Education in the discipline emphasizes "construction procedures, methods, costs, schedules and personnel management," with the objective to deliver a project on time, within budget, and of the desired quality. It integrates engineering design with cost estimating, scheduling, contracts, safety, and resource coordination across a project's lifecycle. The Library of Congress Classification places the related literature under the heading "Building construction," reflecting the discipline's grounding in how civil works are physically realized.

label: Telecommunications Engineering
summary: Telecommunications engineering is a subfield of electrical engineering which seeks to design and devise systems of communication at a distance. The work ranges from basic circuit design to strategic mass developments. A telecommunication engineer is responsible for designing and overseeing the installation of telecommunications equipment and facilities, such as complex electronic switching systems, optical fiber cabling, IP networks, and microwave transmission systems. The discipline also overlaps with broadcast engineering. Its subject matter—telephony, radio, fiber-optic and IP networks, and spectrum use—is coordinated internationally by the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), described as "the United Nations specialized agency for digital technologies (ICTs)."

label: Computer Engineering
summary: Computer engineering is a branch of engineering specialized in developing computer hardware and software. As an engineering discipline at the interface of electrical engineering and computing, it spans digital-logic and circuit design, processor and embedded-system architecture, and the system software that runs on that hardware, distinguishing it from computer science as a practice rooted in engineering design. The professional community is served by the IEEE Computer Society, which describes itself as "Engaging computer engineers, scientists, academia, and industry professionals from all areas of computing," and which sets standards and curricula spanning both hardware and software concepts. Computer engineers work on the design and integration of computing systems rather than on abstract computation alone.

label: Nuclear Engineering
summary: Nuclear engineering is the engineering discipline concerned with designing and applying systems that utilize the energy released by nuclear processes. Its most prominent application is the generation of electricity through nuclear fission. The reaction exploits the nuclear binding energy released when atomic nuclei undergo fission, and nuclear fusion is studied as a further means of generation. The Library of Congress Classification places the field in range TK9001-TK9401, captioned "Nuclear engineering. Atomic power," inside the class TK1-TK9971, "Electrical engineering. Electronics. Nuclear engineering." The American Nuclear Society describes itself as "the premier organization for those that embrace the nuclear sciences and technologies for their vital contributions to improving people's lives and preserving the planet."

label: Robotics
summary: Robotics is the interdisciplinary study and practice of the design, construction, operation, and use of robots. It usually combines four aspects of design work: a power source, mechanical construction, a control system, and software, integrating mechanical, electrical, and computing engineering to build machines that can sense and act. The Library of Congress Classification places robots within range TJ210.2-TJ211.495, captioned "Mechanical devices and figures. Automata. Ingenious mechanisms. Robots (General)," which sits under the mechanical-engineering class TJ1-TJ1570. The IEEE Robotics and Automation Society, the field's principal professional body, states that "Robotics focuses on systems incorporating sensors and actuators that operate autonomously or semi-autonomously in cooperation with humans."

label: Manufacturing Engineering
summary: Manufacturing engineering, also called production engineering, is a branch of professional engineering concerned with planning, developing, and operating the processes and systems that produce goods. It shares concepts with mechanical, chemical, electrical, and industrial engineering, and requires the ability to plan manufacturing practices; to research and develop tools, processes, machines, and equipment; and to integrate facilities and systems for producing quality products with the optimum expenditure of capital. The Library of Congress classifies the subject under "Technology--Manufactures" (class TS). The Society of Manufacturing Engineers, established in 1932, represents the manufacturing industry across North America, including manufacturers, academia, professionals, and students.

label: Metallurgy
summary: Metallurgy is the science and technology of metals, studying the physical and chemical behavior of metallic elements, their inter-metallic compounds, and their mixtures, known as alloys. The discipline divides broadly into extractive metallurgy and physical metallurgy. Extractive metallurgy is a branch of metallurgical engineering studying the process and methods of extracting metals from their natural mineral deposits, addressing ore types, concentration, separation, and chemical processes to produce pure metals and alloys. Physical and process metallurgy covers metallography, heat treating, corrosion, surface engineering, welding and joining, and mechanical testing, applied to materials such as aluminum, titanium, nonferrous alloys, irons, and steels. The Library of Congress classifies metallurgy at TN600-TN799 under "Technology--Mining engineering. Metallurgy." ASM International is the world's largest association of materials-centric engineers and scientists.

label: Mining Engineering
summary: Mining engineering is the engineering discipline concerned with the extraction of minerals from the ground. It is associated with many other disciplines, such as mineral processing, exploration, excavation, geology, metallurgy, geotechnical engineering, and surveying. A mining engineer may manage any phase of mining operations, from exploration and discovery of the mineral resources, through feasibility study, mine design, development of plans, production and operations, to mine closure. The Society for Mining, Metallurgy & Exploration organizes the field into technical divisions spanning Coal & Energy, Environmental, Health & Safety, Industrial Minerals & Aggregates, Mineral & Metallurgical Processing, Mining & Exploration, and Underground Construction, and serves "the mining, resources and underground construction communities." The Library of Congress classifies mining engineering and metallurgy in class TN.

label: Petroleum Engineering
summary: Petroleum engineering is a field of engineering concerned with the activities related to the production of hydrocarbons, which can be either crude oil or natural gas or both. The discipline operates within the upstream sector of the oil and gas industry, covering exploration and production. While geology and geophysics provide static descriptions of reservoir rock, petroleum engineering specializes in estimating recoverable volumes and understanding how oil, water, and gas behave in porous rock under pressure. The Library of Congress classifies the subject at TN860-TN879.5 as "Petroleum. Petroleum engineering," within the broader class for mining engineering and metallurgy. The Society of Petroleum Engineers is described as "the largest individual-member organization serving engineers, scientists, managers and other professionals in the upstream segment of the oil and gas industry."

label: Nanotechnology
summary: Nanotechnology is the manipulation of matter with at least one dimension sized from 1 to 100 nanometers. At this scale, commonly known as the nanoscale, surface area and quantum mechanical effects become important in describing properties of matter. The U.S. National Nanotechnology Initiative notes that "working at the nanoscale enables scientists to understand and utilize the unique physical, chemical, mechanical, and optical properties of materials that occur at this scale." The discipline spans the synthesis, characterization, and engineering of nanoscale structures and devices, drawing on chemistry, physics, materials science, and engineering. Applications include nanomaterials, electronics, medicine, energy, and catalysis, where nanoscale control yields behavior unavailable in bulk matter.

label: Systems Engineering
summary: Systems engineering is an interdisciplinary field of engineering and engineering management that focuses on how to design, integrate, and manage complex systems over their life cycles. It uses systems-thinking principles to organize the systems engineering body of knowledge, and the resulting engineered system can be defined as a combination of components that work in synergy to collectively perform a useful function. Rather than optimizing parts in isolation, the discipline coordinates requirements, architecture, interfaces, verification, and operations across a system's whole life cycle, from concept through retirement. The international professional society for the discipline is the International Council on Systems Engineering (INCOSE).

label: Geomatics
summary: Geomatics is the engineering discipline concerned with measuring, managing, and analyzing spatial and geographic data. Wikipedia, citing the ISO/TC 211 series of standards, defines geomatics as the "discipline concerned with the collection, distribution, storage, analysis, processing, presentation of geographic data or geographic information." The field is an umbrella for land surveying, geodesy, photogrammetry and remote sensing, Geographic Information Systems (GIS), cartography, satellite positioning (GNSS), and hydrography. It serves as the engineering-side home of geodesy, supplying the spatial reference frameworks and measurements on which mapping, navigation, and infrastructure siting depend. The Library of Congress Classification treats the foundational practice under "Surveying" within civil engineering (range TA501–TA625). Geomatics evolved from traditional surveying through integration with computing, providing the spatial-data backbone for civil and environmental projects.

label: Photonics
summary: Photonics is the science and engineering of generating, detecting, and manipulating light in the form of photons—through emission, transmission, modulation, signal processing, switching, amplification, and sensing. It underpins technologies such as lasers, optical fibers and optical communication, photodetectors, displays, and optical sensing. Photonics coexists with optics; there is no widespread agreement on a sharp boundary between the two, and the term gained currency as photon-based devices and systems matured. The discipline is represented by professional societies including SPIE, "the largest global optics and photonics professional society," and Optica (formerly OSA), "the society dedicated to promoting the generation, application, archiving and dissemination of knowledge in the field."

label: Automotive Engineering
summary: Automotive engineering, along with aerospace engineering and naval architecture, is a branch of vehicle engineering, incorporating elements of mechanical, electrical, electronic, software, and safety engineering as applied to the design, manufacture and operation of motorcycles, automobiles, and trucks and their respective engineering subsystems. The field is research-intensive and applies mathematical models to design, develop, fabricate, and test vehicles or vehicle components from concept to production. The Library of Congress Classification places motor vehicles in range TL1-TL483, captioned "Motor vehicles." The discipline's leading professional body, SAE International, was formerly the Society of Automotive Engineers and "adopted its current name in 2006 to reflect both its international membership and the increased scope of its activities beyond automotive engineering."

label: Textile Engineering
summary: Textile engineering, also termed textile manufacturing, is the engineering discipline concerned with the production and processing of textiles. It is largely based on the conversion of fibre into yarn, then yarn into fabric. These are then dyed or printed and fabricated into cloth, which is converted into useful goods such as clothing, household items, upholstery, and various industrial products. The discipline thus spans fibre science, yarn spinning, fabric formation, and finishing operations including dyeing and printing. The Library of Congress classifies textile industries at TS1300 and above, under "Technology--Manufactures--Textile industries." The Textile Institute, founded in Manchester in 1910, is "the professional body for people and organisations working in the textile, clothing and footwear associated industries worldwide."
